findings.title: Possible NullPointerException when the all-Clients resource does not exist
findings.body: In hasPermission(ClientModel, String), when no client-specific resource exists the code falls back to getResourceTypeResource(...) and immediately calls findByResource(server, resource) without a null check. getResourceTypeResource returns null when the 'Clients' resource is absent, which can happen for realms whose admin-permissions client was created before the Clients resource type was introduced or if the resource was not initialized. This turns a permission check that should deny access into an NPE/500 error. The String-scope overload at line 244 does null-check the same lookup, showing the missing check here.

findings.title: Role-mapping checks ignore manage-clients admins and manage scope
findings.body: canMapRoles, canMapCompositeRoles (line 96), and canMapClientScopeRoles (line 101) only evaluate the exact FGAP scope for the client. Unlike canManage(ClientModel), they do not accept the MANAGE_CLIENTS admin role, and unlike the transitive permission model used elsewhere they do not accept a granted MANAGE scope. Consequently, when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled, a traditional realm admin with manage-clients (or an FGAP admin granted only manage on a client) is denied role/composite/client-scope role mapping operations that were previously allowed, breaking admin functionality for fully privileged admins.

findings.title: getClientsWithPermission includes the all-Clients type resource and misses all-clients grants
findings.body: getClientsWithPermission iterates every resource of type 'Clients', including the synthetic all-clients resource whose name is literally 'Clients', and adds resource.getName() to the returned set of client IDs. Callers expect this set to contain client IDs for filtering client lists. When permission is granted only on the all-clients resource, the method returns {'Clients'} instead of the IDs of all clients, so list filtering can return no clients; when mixed with specific grants it also pollutes the ID set with a non-client identifier. The synthetic type resource must be excluded and an all-clients grant handled separately.

findings.title: getResourceName has no Clients branch
findings.body: getResourceName only translates Users resources: it returns 'All users' for the type resource and the username for a specific user. For the newly added Clients type it falls through to resource.getDisplayName(), which for FGAP-created client resources is not set to the clientId (the resource name is the client's internal UUID). Permission/resource representations for clients will therefore show an opaque UUID or blank display name instead of the clientId, unlike the user behavior this PR extends, making client permissions hard to identify in the authorization UI/API.
